$comment: The App Store's listing rules, from Apple's own pages read on the date in 'checked'. Each rule's 'status' says how sure we are: a rule that isn't 'verified' is reported as a warning whatever its severity. To update a rule, change its values, 'source', 'checked' and 'status' together; never change an 'id' (configs relax rules by id).

rules.note: Falls back to app.name. Apple's 'characters'; how emoji count is unverified.
Changes any time, without review.
Falls back to the locale's shared description.
Plain text only: 'HTML format isn't supported'. Tags show as written.
Counted on the keywords joined with commas and no spaces (how they're sent). Apple's product page guide says 100 characters, the version page 100 bytes: bytes (UTF-8) is the stricter.
Each keyword 'greater than two characters'.
Keywords are separated by commas, so a keyword can't contain one.
Apple's advice: a repeated keyword wastes bytes.
Words already in the name or subtitle are indexed already; the version page says not to repeat the app's or company's name.
Apple's advice: avoid the word 'app' and category names.

rules.item: No other apps' or companies' names, trademarks or celebrities' names in the keywords.

rules.note: Not on an app's first version; required on every later one.

rules.item: What's New lists the version's significant changes specifically; generic text only for bug fixes (guideline 2.3.12).

rules.note: Any language.
The value of the environment variable named by review.contact.phoneEnv, checked at push time: international format with '+' and the country code (numbers-only isn't accepted since 2026-08-19).

rules.item: If anything needs a sign-in, give App Review a demo account that doesn't expire (review.demoAccount).

rules.note: The privacy policy's plain text for Apple TV (a file; Apple TV shows the text, not a link). No length limit is published; texts of over 10,000 characters have been accepted (observed).

rules.item: An Apple TV app that requires a game controller says so in its metadata (guideline 2.4.3).

rules.note: A full URL with its protocol.

rules.item: The support URL leads to real contact information (and a legal address, email and phone where local law requires).

rules.note: Required for iOS and macOS apps; app-level, changes release with the next version.

rules.item: Open every URL: App Review does, and a dead link is a rejection. (Scripts here don't reach the network.)

rules.note: Apple's form is the year and the holder: '2026 Example Studio'.
App Store Connect adds the copyright symbol itself.

Guideline 2.3.7: no prices or price claims in the name, subtitle, screenshots and previews (and no pricing packed into keywords). Not banned in the description or promotional text, which may describe a free trial. 'free' also matches 'gluten-free': relax by id when it isn't a price.
Guideline 2.3.10: no names of other mobile platforms or alternative app marketplaces (status bars and imagery in screenshots too). fastlane precheck's other_platforms.
Guideline 2.3.10's 'irrelevant information': desktop and game stores aren't named in the guideline, so a warning; drop it if they are relevant (for example a cross-platform save).
Naming Xbox or PlayStation controllers is common; whether App Review rules on it is unverified (2.4.3 says 'third-party game controllers').
Guideline 2.3.8: 'For Kids' and 'For Children' are reserved for the Kids category.
Guideline 2.3.7: no unverifiable product claims in the subtitle, and nothing but the app's name in the name.
Guideline 2.3.7 asks for accurate metadata; a claim you can back up (with its source) is fine.

Apple-designated features and awards ('Editors' Choice', 'App of the Day', Apple Design Awards) only when Apple gave them, worded as Apple's marketing guidelines say. Not in the guidelines' text read 2026-11-14.
Guidelines 2.1 and 2.2: nothing unfinished. Not re-read on 2026-11-14. fastlane precheck's placeholder_text.
Guideline 2.2: no betas, demos or test versions. fastlane precheck's test_words.
Asset best practices: no website URLs in screenshots and other assets.
Asset best practices: no copyright symbols in screenshots and other assets.
1 to 10 per display type, per locale.
JPEG or PNG; 'Images can't include alpha channels or transparencies' (since 2026-07-08). No colour space or file size stated.
A picture must match one of its platform's slot sizes exactly.

'iPhone: At least one screenshot for iPhone with Dynamic Island (medium display)' (1179x2556 or 1206x2622). Apple's page also keeps scaled fallbacks from the large sets, so a 6.9-inch set alone may be accepted: unverified. Relax this by id only once App Store Connect has taken a listing without it.

Apple's page still says Face ID large is 'Required if app runs on iPhone and screenshots for iPhone with Dynamic Island (large display) aren't provided'. The page contradicts its own medium-display rule.
Required if the app runs on iPad.
A watch app needs one Apple Watch set (any one of these display types).

rules.item: Use the same Apple Watch screenshot size in every localisation.

rules.note: Required from April 2027: Apple's screenshot page says for apps built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later, its news says for every submission. One set (APP_IPHONE_DUO) takes both postures. Plan for every iPhone app.

rules.item: More than half of each set (per device, per locale) shows the app in use; the rest may be marketing art. Never only a sign-in or splash screen; nothing that misrepresents the UI. A panorama across screenshots is fine.
Text and image overlays don't obscure the app's primary functionality.
Screenshots and previews suit a 4+ audience even when the app is rated higher (guideline 2.3.8).
Accounts and personal data shown are fictional, not a real person's; you hold the rights to everything shown (guideline 2.3.9).
No other mobile platforms' devices, icons or status bars in screenshots or previews (guideline 2.3.10).

Apple's product bezels, if used, are the user's own download, used as they are: no tilting, cropping, reflections, shadows or 3D renders, nothing over the device, latest-generation devices. A drawn device simulates no Apple product: none of the details unique to Apple's (Home button, sensor housing, Ring/Silent switch, volume controls).
rules.note: The marketing guidelines say so; whether App Review enforces it on screenshots is unverified (tilted and cropped frames are common in live listings).
Optional; up to 3 per display type and locale.

H.264 (up to High Profile Level 4.0, 10-12 Mbps) in .mov/.m4v/.mp4, or ProRes 422 HQ only in .mov; at most 30 fps; 15-30 s; at most 500 MB (counted as 500,000,000 bytes); stereo audio 44.1 or 48 kHz (AAC 256 kbps, or PCM with ProRes). Sizes are each slot's preview sizes; Mac, Apple TV and Vision Pro landscape only. The poster frame defaults to 5 s. Processing takes up to 24 hours.
Uploads without an audio track are reported to fail processing; add a silent stereo track. Apple's page gives the audio format but doesn't say a track is required.

rules.item: Previews use only screen captures of the app itself (narration and overlays are fine); no hands, devices or footage from elsewhere (guideline 2.3.4).

rules.note: App Store Connect's category ids (the API's appCategories); the names are on Apple's categories page, the ids as the API returns them.
Only Games and Stickers have subcategories; each must belong to its parent (categories.subcategories[parent]).
Up to two Games subcategories.
Each attribute name and value as the API's AgeRatingDeclaration takes it (ageRating.attributes).
Every app needs an age rating ('Unrated' can't be published); push.py sends it only with --age-rating.

rules.item: 'Contests' includes sport or fitness contests and competing for rankings, rewards or personal goals, not only sweepstakes.

slots.$comment: App Store Connect's screenshot display types. Sizes are portrait [w, h]; either orientation is accepted unless 'orientation' says otherwise ('asListed': exactly the sizes written). A picture's slot is found by its pixel size among the slots of its platform; where a size fits more than one slot (2048x2732 fits both 13-inch slots), the first listed wins. 'fallsBackTo': the slot whose pictures App Store Connect scales down when this one has none. 'preview': the slot's app preview type and accepted video sizes.

APP_IPHONE_67.device: iPhone with Dynamic Island, large display (6.9-inch: Air, Pro Max, Plus models)
APP_IPHONE_67.note: Not required by itself: the required iPhone set is the medium one (APP_IPHONE_61). App Store Connect scales the largest set down for the sizes it fills in.

APP_IPHONE_65.device: iPhone with Face ID, large display (6.5-inch: 14 Plus, 11-13 Pro Max, 11, XS Max, XR)
APP_IPHONE_65.note: Apple's page also says it is required when the app runs on iPhone and no Dynamic Island large set is given (rule apple.screenshots.iphone_65.required).

APP_IPHONE_61.device: iPhone with Dynamic Island, medium display (6.1/6.3-inch: Pro, base 15-18, 14 Pro)
APP_IPHONE_61.note: Apple's screenshot page: 'At least one screenshot for iPhone with Dynamic Island (medium display)'. The same page keeps scaled fallbacks, so a 6.9-inch set alone may still be accepted: unverified, so make this set. The display type's mapping to this device class is by name only (the API enum has no descriptions).

APP_IPHONE_58.device: iPhone with Face ID, medium display (5.8/6.1-inch: 16e/17e, 11-14 base, X, XS, 11 Pro)
APP_IPHONE_58.note: Display type mapping by name only (unverified).

APP_IPHONE_55.device: iPhone with Home button, large display (5.5-inch: 6-8 Plus)

APP_IPHONE_47.device: iPhone with Home button, medium display (4.7-inch: SE 2nd/3rd gen, 6-8)

APP_IPHONE_35.note: App previews aren't supported at this size (the API's IPHONE_35 preview type exists but Apple's preview page lists no size).

preview.note: 886x1920 or 1920x886 (App Store Connect's iPhone Duo media page). Apple's one IPHONE_DUO preview set, up to 3.

IPHONE_DUO_OUTER.note: Folded (the cover display). Apple has one iPhone Duo set for both postures: ScreenshotDisplayType APP_IPHONE_DUO takes 1398x2034 and 2853x2007 either way round, up to 10 mixed (App Store Connect's media page; the API answered with APP_IPHONE_DUO and IPHONE_DUO among its valid values on 2026-11-24, though OpenAPI spec 4.6.1 doesn't list them). This slot and IPHONE_DUO_INNER share the type: listing.py builds them as one set, in the shots' order, and counts them together. Required from April 2027 (rule apple.screenshots.iphone_duo.required). The key is ours.

preview.note: 886x1920 or 1920x886 (App Store Connect's iPhone Duo media page). Apple's one IPHONE_DUO preview set, up to 3.

IPHONE_DUO_INNER.note: Open (the inner display). The same Apple set as IPHONE_DUO_OUTER (APP_IPHONE_DUO): see its note. The key is ours.

APP_IPAD_PRO_3GEN_129.note: Required when the app runs on iPad.

APP_IPAD_PRO_129.note: Same pixel size as the 13-inch slot: a 2048x2732 picture goes to APP_IPAD_PRO_3GEN_129 (listed first) unless the config says otherwise.

APP_IPAD_PRO_3GEN_11.note: iPad mini (A20 Pro) sizes added 2026-11-03 (release notes).

APP_WATCH_ULTRA.note: Watch screenshots are part of the iOS version. Use one Watch size across every localisation. Which display type takes Ultra 3/4's 422x514 is by name only (unverified).

design.$comment: What the store allows in a screenshot's design, read by store-screenshots (check.py, sheet.py). Each entry: 'value', where it's written ('source'), when it was read ('checked'), how sure we are ('status'), and 'severity': how check.py reports a picture that breaks it (an entry that isn't verified is reported as a warning whatever its severity). 'bySlot' overrides an entry for some of this file's slots. Values: frames, backgrounds and captions are allowed | discouraged | required | forbidden (captions also oneUnaltered: at least one shot with no words or art over the app); awards are allowed | verifiableOnly | forbidden; deviceArt is ownAsIs (a maker's device art only as the user supplies it, unmodified) | none | allowed; maxTextShare and inUseMajority are shares of the picture or set (0-1); uiFirst is a number of leading shots. Change an entry's value, source, checked and status together.

frames.note: App Review's screenshot guidance (2.3.3) allows text and image overlays and says nothing about device frames; framed screenshots, drawn and tilted ones included, are common in live listings. A drawn frame mustn't simulate an Apple device: see deviceArt.

backgrounds.note: 2.3.3: more than half of a set shows the app in use; the rest may be marketing art, splash screens or marketing text, so a designed background around the app is fine.

captions.note: 2.3.3: screenshots may include text and image overlays as long as the app's primary functionality isn't obscured. Asset best practices: a short phrase that enhances the visual rather than describes it, localised; no prices, discounts, website URLs or copyright symbols (the captions' word and pattern rules).

awards.note: Asset best practices: no unverifiable awards and no Apple-designated recognitions (Editors' Choice, App of the Day, Apple Design Award), and don't spend a whole screenshot on accolades or calls to action. A real third-party award you can show is tolerated (common in live listings). Laurels drawn in the art are for a person to judge.

deviceArt.note: Apple's product bezels only as the user downloads them (the Apple Design Resources licence lets no one redistribute them, and limits them to software that runs only on Apple's platforms), used as is: no tilting, 3D, cropping by the edge (framed-bleed), callouts over the device, shadows or reflections; the latest devices. check.py refuses tilt, 3D, crop and callout overlap on a frame whose JSON says "maker": "apple". A drawn device mustn't copy details unique to Apple products (Home button, sensor housing, Ring/Silent switch, volume controls). Whether App Review enforces the marketing guidelines on screenshots is unverified; the licence applies regardless.

inUseMajority.note: App Review approves only submissions where more than half of the screenshots show the app in use, judged per device set and locale. Never only a sign-in or splash screen. check.py counts the layouts that show a capture (every layout but hero); a person confirms the captures really are the app in use.

categories.$comment: App Store Connect's category ids (status observed: the ids as the API's appCategories returns them; the names are on Apple's categories page). 'Kids' is set through Made for Kids (ageRating.kidsAgeBand), not chosen here; Safari Extensions' id is unverified and left out.

ageRating.$comment: The age rating declaration's attributes as App Store Connect's API takes them (AgeRatingDeclarationUpdateRequest, read 2026-11-14). Frequency attributes accept all five values in the API; which pair the questionnaire shows for each (INFREQUENT_OR_MILD/FREQUENT_OR_INTENSE or INFREQUENT/FREQUENT) is unverified. Ratings: 4+, 9+, 13+, 16+, 18+, Unrated. 'group' is the questionnaire's section.

socialMediaAgeRestricted.note: Social media turned off for users under 13.

contests.note: Infrequent 4+, frequent 13+. Includes sport and fitness contests and competing for rankings or rewards.

kidsAgeBand.note: null when not made for kids; can't be undone once approved.

gracRatingClassificationNumber.note: Korea's GRAC classification number, when required.

creative.$comment: The App Store's creative assets (iOS 27 / iPadOS 27 and later): the product page header and the search results asset, one each per version localization, sent through the App Asset Library (an image, then a placement). Specs from the API's appAssetLibraryRefData and Apple's creative asset specifications page; the art safe area is where everything that must be seen goes (the rest is cropped on some devices and orientations).
